title: A little game, an enormous quarrel
literal_meaning: From a game of jhimiti to the Mahabharata.
explanation: A small disagreement grows into an outsized conflict. The Mahabharata provides a culturally recognisable scale of conflict. The expression is not evidence that the epic war literally began with this named game, and the game’s precise historical rules have not been established here.
usage_example: Two friends disagree over a turn in a game; soon several families are arguing. A neighbour uses the saying to describe how far the quarrel has grown. (New editorial example, not a collected quotation.)
cultural_context: ଝିମିଟି is retained rather than replaced by an invented modern game. The contrast is between a modest starting point and epic-scale escalation.

witnesses.note: Text and accompanying sense read in original community page; rewritten explanation, not historical-origin claim.

origin_note: First coinage, named author and regional distribution are not established. This entry records a contemporary digital witness; it does not prove exclusive Odia origin. No oral-history interview has been conducted.
